subject: Probe-to-Commit: clearance steps, smoke hypotheses & cutover runway
messages:
From: Maya Srinivasan <maya.srinivasan@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Ellis <jordan.ellis@aureliahealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Probe-to-Commit: clearance steps, smoke hypotheses & cutover runway

Hi Jordan — great to meet you on the call this morning. Per our discussion, I put together a short mutual action map draft and an initial set of smoke hypotheses so we have a concrete probe-to-commit path. Attaching two artifacts: the MAP draft (one page) and a lightweight smoke-test CSV you can run during the trial.

High-level asks from Aurelia to validate fit during the trial:
- 2 weeks of representative traffic (batch + API) covering at least 3 common intents
- Target 95th pct latency under 450ms for 128-token responses (on our Dedicated config)
- Concordance >= 85% against your manual samples (we'll share scoring prompts)

Key Redwood-owned exit gates we propose for the trial to consider it a POE (proof of experience):
1) Smoke test pass: zero show-stoppers in the smoke test matrix
2) Latency envelope confirmed under load (simple load run)
3) No critical security blockers (we'll provide SOC2 controls evidence)

Next steps I recommend:
- You review the MAP and smoke hypotheses and flag any missing success signals by EOD Wed (4/7)
- If agreed, we lock in the two-week trial window starting Mon 4/12 and schedule a cutover readiness check on day +10

Attachment stubs: 20270405_MAP_draft.xlsx (MAP one-pager), smoke_test_hypotheses.csv

Thanks — Maya

Maya Srinivasan
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Ellis <jordan.ellis@aureliahealth.com>
To: Maya Srinivasan <maya.srinivasan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya@aureliahealth.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 12:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Probe-to-Commit: clearance steps, smoke hypotheses & cutover runway

Thanks Maya — this is exactly the level of clarity we need. Quick notes from our side after reading the attachments: 
- The traffic window looks fine; we'll reserve 4/12–4/23 but need to confirm sample size of production-like intent distribution (Priya will confirm).
- Latency target: 450ms at 95th is aggressive but reasonable if we run the Dedicated config you suggested. We do want a secondary SLA for 99th pct under 800ms.
- Concordance: we can commit to running the concordance scoring if you provide the scoring prompts & rubric.

We have two procurement asks before we start the trial: a short mutual NDA addendum for analytics sharing, and a simple procurement form for a short-term reserved capacity commitment. I’ll attach the procurement form later today.

Can you confirm Redwood will provide the smoke test harness and a short playbook for running the load run? Also — please include a rollback / fallthrough clause in the MAP if we identify a critical model regression during the trial.

— Jordan

Jordan Ellis
Head of AI Ops, Aurelia Health
jordan.ellis@aureliahealth.com | (646) 555-0133
From: Maya Srinivasan <maya.srinivasan@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Ellis <jordan.ellis@aureliahealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 6 Apr 2027 08:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Probe-to-Commit: clearance steps, smoke hypotheses & cutover runway

Jordan — thanks, and yes to all of the above. Quick clarifications: 
- We’ll add 99th pct under 800ms as a monitoring sentinel (not a hard reject gate for the initial prove-out) but include it in the post-trial SLA discussion.
- I’ve updated the MAP to include a rollback/fallthrough lane that triggers on any critical regression (concordance drop >10 points or critical latency blowout). The rollback lane includes immediate fallback to a smaller quantized model variant and an ops playbook run.
- Redwood will provide the smoke test harness (simple CLI + a CSV of test cases) and a short load-run playbook — see Drive link in the metadata. Ben will own the smoke harness delivery and the load-run on our side.

Ben / Mateo — can you both confirm ownership of the deliverables and estimate ETA? We’re aiming to share the final MAP with Aurelia by Wed EOD (4/7).

Thanks — Maya

On Tue, Apr 6, 2027 at 09:02 AM Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Maya — I’ll own the smoke harness and the 2-hour load run script. ETA for artifacts to you: 4/7 10:00 PDT. I’ll include a README with the exact commands and expected metrics.

>

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 7 Apr 2027 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Probe-to-Commit: clearance steps, smoke hypotheses & cutover runway

Jordan / team — attaching the smoke harness stub (referenced README) and the quick-run load script. Attachment stubs: smoke_test_hypotheses.csv, load_run_readme.md.

Brief on expected outputs from the load run:
- 90th/95th/99th latency percentiles for a 30-minute ramp (baseline config + Dedicated pool)
- Token throughput and GPU utilization summary
- Any decoding divergence cases flagged for manual review

If the smoke matrix has no showstoppers and the 95th stays <450ms, we recommend greenlighting the production-mirroring stage. If the 99th exceeds 800ms repeatedly, we’ll engage the rollback lane and route traffic to a lighter model variant.

I’ll be available for the run and can join your ops channel for the day-of.

— Ben

Ben Carter
SRE & Trials Lead, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai
From: Maya Srinivasan <maya.srinivasan@redwood.ai>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai>, Priya Rao <priya@aureliahealth.com>
Date: Wed, 7 Apr 2027 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Probe-to-Commit: clearance steps, smoke hypotheses & cutover runway

Jordan / Priya — thanks for the quick turn. Per the thread, final decisions and next steps we have agreed to: 
- Trial window: Mon 4/12 -> Fri 4/23 (2-week probe-to-commit).
- Deliverables pre-trial (due Thu 4/8 EOD): final MAP PDF, smoke harness + README, concordance scoring prompts, NDA addendum (procurement team).
- Acceptance / exit gates for a POE: 
  * All smoke-test critical checks = pass (no showstoppers)
  * 95th pct latency <= 450ms for representative runs during load test
  * Concordance >= 85% on agreed scoring rubric
  * No unresolved critical security controls (SOC2 evidence acceptable)
- Fallback: If critical regressions appear (concordance drop >10 pts or 99th >800ms persistent), we will trigger rollback lane and a joint incident review within 24 hours.

Jordan — if that matches your reading, please reply with a one-line ack and we’ll lock calendars. We’ll post the final MAP and the harness to the Drive link and share the HubSpot deal update after your ack.

Best — Maya
